threads.body: In the experimental async streaming path, input_messages/system_instruction are built unconditionally. Other paths guard this behind _content_recording_enabled to avoid capturing potentially sensitive content and doing unnecessary work when content capture is disabled. Align this branch with the same conditional behavior.

threads.body: Setting OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_EMIT_EVENT in-process mutates global environment and overrides user configuration for the whole application (and any other instrumentations). Prefer relying on opentelemetry-util-genai's default emit-event behavior (derived from content capture mode), or make event emission an explicit option rather than force-setting an env var here.

threads.body:
Arguments/result are serialized after the tool executes. This means arguments won't be recorded on exceptions, and it does extra json.dumps work even when content capture is disabled. Consider setting tool_invocation.arguments before invoking the tool (so failures still have args) and only computing/setting arguments/result when tool_invocation.should_capture_content_on_span is true.

This issue also appears on line 96 of the same file.

threads.body: This test calls self.setUp()/self.tearDown() manually inside the loop, but TestCase doesn't define tearDown(), so the installed OTelMocker providers are never restored between iterations. This can leak global OTel state across subtests. Consider adding a tearDown that calls self._otel.uninstall(), and in this test explicitly uninstall/reinstall (or refactor to construct a fresh OTelMocker/TelemetryHandler without calling setUp directly).
